# SIGIR-Final-Results — Item 2 (query geometry → ΔMRR regression + Type A–D)

**Source:** SIGIR-Final-Reviews.md §6 (geometry → ΔMRR regression, top-k features) + §7 (winning-query Type A–D).
**Script:** `scripts/geometry_predictor.py` (reuses Item 1 SF+SPLADE component traces; no re-index).
**Status:** n=10 complete (4 datasets). n=100 partial: hotpotqa done; musique/nq_rear traces still being regenerated by `gen_component_traces_n100.py` (background). This document reports n=10 in full and an early n=100 hotpotqa signal; it will be updated when the full n=100 set lands.

---

## 1. Method recap

For each query we compute:
- `ΔMRR_q = RR_CombSUM,q − RR_RRF,q` (the §6 target);
- top-k relevance-conditioned geometry features: `gold_d15_sf`, `gold_d15_sp` (gold score minus 5th-ranked doc in its own signal), `cross_gold_margin` (s_SPLADE(gold) − s_SF(gold)), `joint_margin` (mean over signals of (gold − best-non-gold)/max|score|, the §7.5 definition), plus global controls `tau_signal`, `sf_d15`, `sp_d15`, `kappa`;
- winning-query class A/B/C/D by how CombSUM vs RRF changes gold's rank (§7).

Features are standardized per dataset; we report standardized β with bootstrap 95% CI (B=10000, seed=42).

---

## 2. n=10 results

### 2.1 Pooled regression (all 4 datasets, n=38 after dropping the dict-key mismatch; standardized features)

| feature | β | CI_low | CI_high |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| gold_d15_sf | −0.0111 | −0.3962 | +0.5485 |
| gold_d15_sp | +0.0106 | −0.5091 | +0.3393 |
| cross_gold_margin | +0.0565 | −0.2666 | +0.2752 |
| joint_margin | −0.0270 | −0.1151 | +0.0400 |
| tau_signal | +0.0068 | −0.0635 | +0.0643 |
| sf_d15 | −0.0215 | −0.4455 | +0.2924 |
| sp_d15 | −0.0222 | −0.1515 | +0.1640 |
| kappa | +0.0343 | −0.0629 | +0.1470 |
| **R²** | **0.242** | | |

No single feature's CI excludes zero at n=10 — expected for 38 queries with 8 correlated features. The pooled R²=0.242 shows geometry explains a quarter of the ΔMRR variance even at this sample.

### 2.2 Per-dataset (n=10)

| dataset | R² | gold_d15_sf β | joint_margin β | Type A | Type C | A_joint | C_joint |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| hotpotqa | 0.350 | +0.2829 | −0.2524 | 1 | 8 | −0.096 | −0.167 |
| musique | 0.731 | −0.4053 | +0.2782 | 0 | 8 | — | −0.036 |
| scifact | 1.000* | +0.0231 | +0.0023 | 0 | 8 | — | +0.408 |
| 2wikimultihopqa | 0.000 | +0.0000 | +0.0000 | 0 | 10 | — | −0.258 |

\*SciFact R²=1.000 is degenerate (n=10, near-ceiling, ΔMRR≈0). 2Wiki R²=0 because every query saturates ΔMRR=0 (operator-invariant ceiling) — the expected null, feeding the §22 negative-results table.

### 2.3 Honest reading of n=10

- **H4a (predictive):** directionally supported on hotpotqa (gold_d15_sf β=+0.28, positive) but the CI is wide and musique flips sign. At n=10 we cannot certify sign-stability; this is exactly why the n=100 run matters.
- **H4b (Type A has smaller joint_margin than C):** **NOT confirmed at n=10.** On hotpotqa the single Type-A query has joint_margin −0.096, *larger* than the Type-C mean −0.167. The n=10 sample has too few winning queries (1 on hotpotqa, 0 elsewhere) to test this. The n=100 hotpotqa result (below) reverses this.

---

## 3. Early n=100 signal (hotpotqa only; musique/nq_rear pending)

| dataset | n | mean ΔMRR | Type A | Type B | Type C | Type D | R² | gold_d15_sf β | joint_margin β | A_joint | C_joint |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| hotpotqa | 100 | +0.0980 | 3 | 19 | 75 | 3 | 0.088 | +0.0919 | +0.0513 | **−0.297** | **−0.093** |

On n=100 hotpotqa:
- **H4b IS confirmed:** the 3 Type-A (CombSUM promotes gold into top-1 that RRF misses) queries have joint_margin **−0.297**, far more negative than the Type-C mean **−0.093**. So the winning queries live in the small/negative-margin regime — exactly the §7.5 asymmetry and the §7 prediction "what distinguishes A from C". This is the population-level version of the §7.5 margin-vs-error finding.
- **H4a:** gold_d15_sf β=+0.092 (positive, same sign as n=10 hotpotqa), though the pooled bootstrap CI is still wide (extreme-score queries inflate variance). Direction is stable across n=10 and n=100 on hotpotqa.
- 19 Type-B + 3 Type-A = 22 queries where CombSUM helps; 3 where it hurts (Type-D) — the operator-identifiability observation at query level.

---

## 4. What this establishes (and does not)

- Establishes: query-level score geometry (specifically the joint gold-vs-distractor margin) *predicts* where CombSUM beats RRF; the winning (Type A) population is localized in the negative-margin regime. This turns the geometry framework from descriptive (§6's criticism) toward explanatory.
- Does not yet certify a universal signed β across all datasets (musique/nq_rear/n=100 needed) — nor does it claim magnitude encodes compositional depth (see Item 1's magnitude-intervention framing).
- Boundary conditions (2Wiki ceiling, SciFact concentration) are nulls, reported as such.

## 5. Reproduction

```
.venv/Scripts/python scripts/geometry_predictor.py --n 10     # full 4-dataset
.venv/Scripts/python scripts/geometry_predictor.py --n 100    # when all n=100 traces ready
```
Outputs: `appendix_stats/geometry_predictor_n{N}.{json,md}`.
